title: Missing transaction reminder (spec 001)
description: Implement specs/001-missing-tx-reminder (firefly-jar check/auth/accounts) per tasks.md T001-T083.
design:
The binding specification is the Spec Kit feature directory `specs/001-missing-tx-reminder/`, under the project constitution `.specify/memory/constitution.md` (which wins every conflict):

- spec.md: user stories US1-US4, FR-001..FR-039, SC-001..SC-009.
- plan.md: technical context, package layout, Complexity Tracking (recorded TDD deviations T006, T025).
- research.md: decisions R1-R18 (Enable Banking, Firefly III API details, notifiers, tooling, hints).
- data-model.md: domain types, mapping resolution order, reconcile algorithm steps 1-7, exit rules.
- contracts/: cli.md, config.md, digest.md, state.md.
- tasks.md: the task contract T001-T083; each task bead's design holds its task text verbatim.

Product in one paragraph: firefly-jar is a one-shot Go CLI run by cron. `check` fetches recent bank transactions via Enable Banking, compares them with a self-hosted Firefly III (read-only), and sends a Telegram/email digest listing bank transactions nobody entered. It never creates, edits or deletes anything in Firefly III or at the bank. Exit 0 clean, 1 missing found, 2 failed or partial (2 wins). `auth <bank>` creates a bank consent session; `accounts` lists bank-to-Firefly account mapping.
notes:
Global Constraints (from tasks.md "Conventions every task follows" and .claude/CLAUDE.md):

1. Read-only: the Firefly client exposes list methods only; its transport rejects every method except GET before the request leaves the process (constitution I; HEAD removed by ruling on fj-xwu.12). Bank access is account-information only; no payment endpoints, no Psu-* headers.
2. Nothing dropped silently: len(inWindow) == Matched + Missing + Deduplicated + Void, asserted in every reconcile case. A partial run never exits 0 or 1.
3. Quiet when clean: a check exiting 0 or 1 writes nothing to stdout/stderr; only WARN+ reaches stderr; the full log (JSON) goes to the log file.
4. No scheduler, daemon or HTTP server.
5. Money is never a float (domain.Amount{Value decimal.Decimal; Currency}). Dates are civil dates (internal/civil.Date); Firefly date = YYYY-MM-DD prefix as rendered.
6. Transaction descriptions and counterparty names are never logged at any level. Secrets only from env vars or *_file paths, never in logs/errors/digests. IBANs masked (LT12…3456) wherever they leave the process.
7. Tests: testify suites only; exactly one Test<Pkg> entry per package containing only suite.Run calls; all assertions are suite methods; table cases use s.Run. Retry/backoff timing uses testing/synctest, never real sleeps, and never httptest.Server or sockets inside a bubble (fake RoundTripper or net.Pipe). Golden files regenerate only with UPDATE_GOLDEN=1. Fixtures anonymized.
8. Lint (.golangci.yml is never edited): no package-level var or init(); wrap errors crossing packages; return concrete types; ≤5 exported types per file; filepath.Clean on user-supplied paths before open; 120 columns; comments end with a period; sloglint (injected loggers, lowercase messages, snake_case keys); funcorder; no unnecessary //nolint.
9. Dependencies (owner-approved 2026-09-22): github.com/goccy/go-yaml, github.com/shopspring/decimal, github.com/spf13/cobra (runtime), github.com/stretchr/testify (tests); internal/civil is a trimmed copy of Google's civil.Date. No JWT/HTTP/retry library, no codegen.
10. Gate: `task check` (format:check → lint → test -race) exits 0 at the end of every implementation task.
11. Commits: Conventional Commits, subject and body only — NO Co-Authored-By, NO Claude-Session, no AI or agent trailer. Branch feature/001-missing-tx-reminder. No push, no gh.
12. No tracked file names another project of the author's, a local filesystem path, a real identifier, token or personal email.

`internal/reconcile/reconcile_pkg_test.go`, as table-driven cases. **Every case asserts the invariant**
`len(inWindow) == len(Matched)+len(Missing)+Deduplicated+Void`. Cases:
- Spec US1 scenario 1: −12.40 EUR on 09-20 vs Firefly −12.40 on 09-21, tolerance 3 → matched.
- Scenario 2 → missing.
- Scenario 3: two −5.00 on the same day, one Firefly entry → exactly one missing.
- Scenario 4: pending unmatched → `Missing.Pending`.
- Scenario 5: a transaction on `window.From` → `LastReminder`.
- Tolerance edges: a difference of exactly 3 days matches; 4 does not.
- Greedy order: bank txs on 09-10 and 09-12 with Firefly entries on 09-11 and 09-13 → both match.
- A different currency never matches. A different sign never matches.
- Bank transactions outside the window are excluded from every count.
- `Void` is counted and never missing.
- Deduplication: Pending and Booked with the same `EntryRef`, both in the window → Deduplicated 1, and the
  Booked one is reconciled. If the Booked twin is outside the window, the Pending one stays.
- An empty `EntryRef` never deduplicates.
- FR-010: Firefly entries with no bank counterpart produce no Missing item and no count change.
- Hints (FR-025a, data-model step 6):
  - Bank −4.50 on 09-10 and 09-15, one Firefly −4.50 on 09-13, tolerance 3 → 09-10 is matched. 09-15 is
    missing with `Hint{Kind: Taken, Date: 09-13}`.
  - Bank −9.99 on 09-10, Firefly −9.99 on 09-15, tolerance 3 → missing with `Hint{Kind: NearMiss,
    Date: 09-15}` (5 ≤ 2×3).
  - At 7 days apart there is no hint (7 > 6).
  - A different amount or currency never produces a hint.
  - With two candidates, the nearest wins, then the earlier date, then the lower group id.
  - A Taken candidate beats a NearMiss one at equal distance.
  - Hints never change the matched and missing counts.
- Determinism: shuffled input orders give an identical result, including hints.

Why: constitution Principle II says every bank transaction in the window ends matched, reported, set aside by a documented deterministic rule, or on an account reported as unchecked, and 'every set-aside entry is counted in the run summary'. comments.text:
Spike result (full report):

# fj-91d.6: Spike: replace httpx.RetryTransport with go-retryablehttp or retry-go?

**Recommendation: keep `internal/httpx` and adopt neither library.** No migration bead needed.

Neither library covers the retry contract (R12, FR-031) on its own terms. With go-retryablehttp, every
guarantee still comes from code we write: a `CheckRetry`, a `Backoff`, an `ErrorHandler`, a nil
`Logger`, an inner `*http.Client` with its own `Timeout` and `CheckRedirect`, and an outer wrapper
that keeps POST out. Its defaults also break project invariants: it logs every request to stderr,
retries and replays POST bodies, puts the full URL in errors, and follows redirects inside the
retry layer. retry-go is a clean, dependency-free, MIT-licensed loop. But it knows nothing about HTTP, so the
wrapper stays about the same size. Either migration saves roughly 40-60 lines of production code, saves
no test code, and every one of the 22 behaviour tests would have to be ported.

## Method

- Read `internal/httpx` (retry.go, timeout.go, client.go and their tests), research R12, FR-031, R8, and
  the call sites in `internal/firefly`, `internal/bank/enablebanking` and `internal/app/wire.go`.
- Library docs via ctx7: `/hashicorp/go-retryablehttp` and `/avast/retry-go`. Source read at the latest
  tags (retryablehttp v0.7.8, retry-go v5.0.0). Maturity from the GitHub API and the Go module proxy.
- Built a throwaway spike module outside the repository (repository untouched). It configured each
  library to meet the contract and ran it under `testing/synctest` with an in-process fake
  `http.RoundTripper`. Observed results are quoted below as "spike".

## Maturity and footprint

| | hashicorp/go-retryablehttp | avast/retry-go |
|---|---|---|
| Stars / forks | 2,351 / 299 | 2,962 / 179 |
| License | MPL-2.0 (file-level copyleft; binary distribution must tell recipients where the MPL source is) | MIT |
| Latest release | v0.7.8, 2025-06-18 (proxy time) | v5.0.0, 2025-11-24 |
| Previous releases | v0.7.7 2024-05-30, v0.7.6 2024-05-09 | v4.7.0 2025-10-14, v4.6.1 2025-02-24 |
| Activity since last release | Only compliance headers, CODEOWNERS and dependabot commits (last 2026-04-14). No functional change. | Docs fix (last commit 2026-02-12) |
| Open issues + PRs | 95 | 18 |
| API stability | Pre-1.0 (v0.x) | v5 is a breaking API redesign, 10 months old |
| Runtime deps added to our build | `github.com/hashicorp/go-cleanhttp` v0.5.2, **released 2021-02-03**, MPL-2.0. This fails the "no release older than 2025-01-01" rule, so it would need an explicit owner exception. | None (its only requirement is testify, already ours at v1.12.1) |
| go.sum-only additions (test deps of the library) | go-hclog v1.6.3 (2024-04), fatih/color v1.16.0 (listed in CLAUDE.md as "considered and not adopted"), mattn/go-colorable, mattn/go-isatty, golang.org/x/sys v0.20.0 | None |
| Exposes `http.RoundTripper` | Yes (`retryablehttp.RoundTripper{Client: *Client}`), but it drives a nested `*http.Client`, not a `RoundTripper`. Its own doc says it "doesn't always act exactly as a RoundTripper should". | No. It is a generic `func() error` / `func() (T, error)` loop. |

## Guarantee by option

Legend: **native** = default behaviour already matches. **hook** = achievable only by supplying our own
function to the library. **ours** = must stay in our own wrapper code. **conflict** = the default
violates the guarantee and must be actively overridden.

| # | Guarantee (R12 / FR-031 / invariants) | ours today | go-retryablehttp v0.7.8 | retry-go v5.0.0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | At most 3 retries (4 attempts) | yes | native (`RetryMax: 3`; default is 4) | native (`Attempts(4)`; default is 10) |
| 2 | Retry on network error, any 5xx, 429 | yes | hook. `DefaultRetryPolicy` skips 501, retries status 0, and uses regexes on error strings to skip TLS, scheme, header and redirect errors. Our `CheckRetry` is needed for exact parity. | ours. The attempt func must convert a 5xx/429 *response* into an error to trigger a retry. |
| 3 | Other 4xx never retried | yes | native | ours |
| 4 | Backoff 1 s / 2 s / 4 s with ±20% jitter | yes | hook. `DefaultBackoff` has no jitter. `LinearJitterBackoff` is linear. A custom `Backoff` func is needed. | hook. `BackOffDelay` gives 1/2/4, but `RandomDelay` adds only `[0, MaxJitter)`, not ±20%. A custom `DelayType` is needed. |
| 5 | Retry-After (seconds or HTTP-date) replaces backoff, for any retryable status | yes | partial/hook. Honoured only on 429 and 503, and parsed with `time.RFC1123` only, whereas `http.ParseTime` accepts all three RFC 9110 date forms. A custom `Backoff` is needed. | ours (parse, then carry the delay through a typed error into `DelayType`) |
| 6 | Retry-After capped at 60 s; over-cap → typed `RetryAfterTooLongError` → "rate limited" | yes | **conflict** + hook. Retry-After is **uncapped**: `RetryWaitMax` bounds only the exponential part, so a `Retry-After: 3600` sleeps an hour. `Backoff` cannot return an error. Spike: `CheckRetry` returns `(false, &RetryAfterTooLongError{})` plus a custom `ErrorHandler` that drains the body and returns `nil, err`. `errors.As` then works. | ours (`retry.Unrecoverable(&RetryAfterTooLongError{})`; spike: `errors.As` works) |
| 7 | Only bodyless GET/HEAD retried; POST never (single-use auth code) | yes | **conflict**. The default policy is method-agnostic, and `FromRequest` does `io.ReadAll` on any body and **replays it**. Spike: a POST with a JSON body hit 500 and was retried and succeeded (2 calls). `CheckRetry` gets `(ctx, resp, err)` with no request, and `resp` is nil on network errors, so it cannot decide by method. An outer wrapper of ours has to route non-GET/HEAD requests around the library. | ours (same up-front method/body check) |
| 8 | Per-attempt 30 s timeout including body read; no whole-exchange timeout | yes | native via the nested client's `HTTPClient.Timeout = 30s`. Spike: a hung attempt was cut at 30 s and retried (31 s gap = 30 s + 1 s backoff). The non-retried path (POST) bypasses the library, so `TimeoutTransport` stays anyway. Telegram also uses it directly. | ours (`TimeoutTransport` stays) |
| 9 | Discarded bodies drained, capped at 64 KiB, then closed | yes | partial. Drains intermediate bodies at a **4 KiB** cap. The cap is an unexported package var and not configurable. Draining 4 KiB is acceptable, but the existing cap test changes meaning (it would test library internals). | ours |
| 10 | After the last retry, hand the **last response** back to the caller (enablebanking maps the final 429/5xx status and error body to "rate limited" / "bank error") | yes (`TestGivesUpAfterMaxRetriesReturningTheLastResponse`) | **conflict** + hook. The default drains and closes the last body and returns `"GET <url> giving up after N attempt(s)"`. `PassthroughErrorHandler` can return **both** a response and an error, and then `net/http` calls the global `log.Printf("RoundTripper returned a response & error; ignoring response")` to stderr. Needs a custom `ErrorHandler`. Spike: works. | ours. On failure `Do` returns the zero value, so the wrapper must count attempts itself and stash the last response (spike: works, but awkwardly). |
| 11 | Context cancellation honoured during waits | yes | native (timer + `select` on `req.Context()`). Side effect: calls `CloseIdleConnections()` on the **shared** base transport on every give-up or cancel. | native (`retry.Context(req.Context())`; `LastErrorOnly(true)` returns `context.Cause`) |
| 12 | Testable under `testing/synctest` with in-process RoundTrippers, no sockets, no real sleeps | yes | yes (spike: all scenarios ran in 0.00 s). Uses `time.NewTimer`, and `timeNow` is a package var. Caveat: the nested `http.Client.Timeout` starts a `setRequestCancel` goroutine that lives until the body is closed, so a test that forgets to close a body panics the bubble with "deadlock". | yes (spike). Uses `time.After`. Global `math/rand` only in the unused `RandomDelay`. |
| 13 | Errors carry no secrets and no URL noise | yes (wraps errors with fixed prefixes; enablebanking strips the `*url.Error` shell so the URL is not repeated) | **conflict**. The default error embeds `METHOD <full URL including query>`. `redactURL` masks only a userinfo password. The outer client adds its own `*url.Error`, so the URL appears twice and the `*url.Error` stripping in enablebanking no longer removes it. Needs a custom `ErrorHandler` that returns the raw error. Response bodies are never put in errors (only the status text). | fine. Errors are what we return. The default `retry.Error` concatenates every attempt ("All attempts fail: #1 … #4"), so `LastErrorOnly(true)` is needed. |
| 14 | No global logger; quiet when clean (cron mails any stderr) | yes (no logging) | **conflict**. `NewClient()`, and `RoundTripper{}` with a nil `Client`, use the package global `log.New(os.Stderr, "", log.LstdFlags)`. Spike: one `[DEBUG] GET https://…?query` line per request, plus one per retry, so **every clean cron run would mail**. Avoiding it means building a `Client` literal with `Logger: nil`. In a literal, a nil `CheckRetry` or `Backoff` panics on the first request, so every field must be set. A regression test is needed to pin this. | fine (no logging at all) |
| 15 | No redirects followed (R8: bearer token never replayed) | yes (`NewClient` → `ErrUseLastResponse`) | **conflict**. The nested `http.Client` follows up to 10 redirects by default, *below* our outer client's redirect policy, so it needs its own `CheckRedirect` plus a test. There would be two redirect policies to keep in sync. | n/a (wraps a RoundTripper) |
| 16 | Firefly's `ReadOnlyTransport` stays outermost | yes | yes (it is a RoundTripper; place it under `ReadOnlyTransport`). Any follow-up request the nested client made on its own would never pass back through the guard. With #15 fixed, that is only a GET retry. | yes |

**Tally for go-retryablehttp:** 3 guarantees native (1, 3, 11), 1 native-with-caveat (8), and 6 where the
**default actively violates** the contract or an invariant (6, 7, 10, 13, 14, 15). **retry-go:** 2 native
(1, 11) and no conflicts, but everything HTTP-specific is ours.

## What code would remain ours

**go-retryablehttp.** A wrapper RoundTripper for the GET/HEAD-bodyless bypass. The `Client` literal
(nil `Logger`, `RetryMax`, nested `http.Client` with `Timeout` and `CheckRedirect`). `CheckRetry` (status
set plus the over-cap typed error). `Backoff` (1/2/4 ±20% with an injectable jitter; Retry-After for any
status). `ErrorHandler` (return the last response; return a raw error; drain on over-cap).
`RetryAfterTooLongError`. `parseRetryAfter`. `TimeoutTransport` (bypass path and Telegram). `NewClient`.
What we would delete: the attempt loop, `wait`, and the zero-value default accessors.

**retry-go.** Everything above except the loop and the wait timer. The added pieces are the
response→error→response round trip (a typed status error carrying the Retry-After delay), our own attempt
counter to keep the last response, `LastErrorOnly(true)`, and `Unrecoverable` for the over-cap case.

## Size estimate

Current code: `retry.go` has 273 lines (164 non-comment, non-blank), `timeout.go` 72 (42), `client.go` 23
(12). Tests: `retry_test.go` has 830 lines (605) and `client_test.go` 203 (144), for 22 suite methods in
total (15 + 7).

| | Production code | Test code | Module files |
|---|---|---|---|
| go-retryablehttp | `retry.go` (164 code lines) replaced by an adapter of ~110 code lines (spike was 109 raw lines; about 170-190 lines once lint-compliant and documented). `timeout.go` and `client.go` stay. **Net about −50 to −60 code lines.** | **0 removed.** All 22 tests ported one-to-one (setup changes: no `MaxRetries`/`BaseDelay`/`Jitter`/`AttemptTimeout` fields, and the drain test moves from 64 KiB to the library's fixed 4 KiB). About 4 new guard tests for library traps (no stderr logging, nested client never follows a redirect, POST never buffered or retried, no URL in the error). **Net about +80 to +120 test lines.** | go.mod +2 (one of them the 2021 cleanhttp), go.sum +~14 |
| retry-go | Wrapper of ~110-120 code lines (spike was 80 raw lines without the typed error or the parser). **Net about −40 to −50 code lines.** | 0 removed. 22 ported, +1-2. | go.mod +1, go.sum +2 |

## Recommendation and risks

**Keep ours.** Reasons:

1. **The guarantees are the value, and they stay ours either way.** Retry-After cap, typed over-cap
   error, GET/HEAD-only, last response handed back, per-attempt timeout, drain: each one ends up as our
   hook code under our tests. A library would replace only the ~40-line loop and timer.
2. **go-retryablehttp's defaults conflict with invariants 4 and R8.** Its stderr logger, POST
   body replay, uncapped Retry-After, URL-bearing errors, nested redirect-following client and
   response-dropping error path are each one missed field away from a silent regression. The one that
   matters most for cron is the stderr logger: every clean run would produce mail. We would need extra
   tests just to pin the library's configuration.
3. **Dependency policy.** retryablehttp pulls in go-cleanhttp v0.5.2 (2021), which fails the
   2025-01-01 rule. It adds MPL-2.0 notice obligations, and it is a pre-1.0 package whose repo has had
   only compliance commits since its last release. retry-go passes the policy cleanly, but brings
   almost no net benefit.
4. **Test surface does not shrink.** The bead requires the existing 22 behaviour tests to be kept or
   ported one-to-one, so migration is pure churn in the test suite.

**Risks of keeping ours:** we own about 165 lines of retry logic. This is mitigated by the 22 synctest
suites that already pin every branch. The code is finished, stdlib-only and has no upgrade cadence to
track.

**Risks of adopting (for the record):** go-retryablehttp: a silent stderr-noise regression, redirects
followed inside the retry layer, a policy exception for cleanhttp, MPL, and an upstream in maintenance
mode. retry-go: v5 is a young breaking redesign, and the response→error→response adapter is harder to
read than today's direct loop.

**When to revisit:** if a future adapter needs retried POSTs with body replay, or several independent
retry policies. That is go-retryablehttp's actual strength. If it happens, re-evaluate with the logger,
redirect and error-handler traps above as acceptance tests.

**Suggested follow-up (owner's call):** add a line to research R12 "Alternatives considered" that records
this decision and the reasons above, so the owner's question has a permanent answer in the spec.

comments.text:
Spike result (full report):

# fj-91d.7: use github.com/jarcoal/httpmock for HTTP tests?

## Recommendation: adopt, partial

Add `github.com/jarcoal/httpmock` as a **test-only** dependency (same status as `testify`) and
migrate the pure client-unit-test suites in `internal/firefly`, `internal/bank/enablebanking`, and
the non-timing parts of `internal/notify/telegram` to it. **Keep** the hand-written
`http.RoundTripper` fakes in `internal/httpx` (`RetrySuite`, `ClientSuite`) and in
`internal/notify/telegram`'s timing suite, and **keep** `httptest.Server` in
`internal/app/readonly_test.go` and `internal/app/privacy_test.go`. Reasons and evidence below.

## Facts (checked 2026-09-23)

- Repo: `github.com/jarcoal/httpmock`, MIT license, 2078 stars, not archived, last push
  2026-08-29.
- Releases: v1.4.2 (2026-07-28), v1.4.1 (2025-08-19), v1.4.0 (2025-04-05) — all ≥ 2025-01-01, no
  pseudo-version needed.
- `go.mod` requires `go 1.18`; no conflict with this repo's `go 1.27.1`.
- Transitive dependency footprint: httpmock's own `go.mod` declares one `require`,
  `github.com/maxatome/go-testdeep v1.14.0` (plus its indirect `github.com/davecgh/go-spew
  v1.1.1`) — but `go list -deps github.com/jarcoal/httpmock` (verified in a scratch module) shows
  the package itself imports **only the standard library**. `go-testdeep`/`go-spew` are httpmock's
  *own* test dependencies; they land in a consumer's `go.sum` (for module-graph verification) but
  are never compiled into a consumer's build or test binary. Net added build/test dependency
  surface for firefly-jar: zero third-party packages.
- Library docs consulted via `ctx7` (`npx ctx7@latest library httpmock ...` →
  `/jarcoal/httpmock`, then two `docs` calls) for: per-client `NewMockTransport` vs.
  `DefaultTransport`, call counting/inspection, file-based responders, sequential responders
  (`ResponderFromMultipleResponses`), and header/query matchers (`RegisterMatcherResponder`,
  `RegisterResponderWithQuery`).

### Spike: does it work inside `testing/synctest`?

Verified empirically in a throwaway module (not in this repo): `httpmock.NewMockTransport()` used
as an `http.Client.Transport` works correctly **inside a `synctest.Test` bubble**, including a case
where the round trip happens from a goroutine spawned inside the bubble after a `time.Sleep`. All
of the following passed under `go test -race`:

- A synchronous round trip inside the bubble.
- A round trip after `time.Sleep(1s)` in the bubble's main goroutine, with the responder observing
  `time.Now()` correctly advanced by the bubble's fake clock.
- The same, from a spawned goroutine, synchronized with `synctest.Wait()` + a `done` channel.
- `GetCallCountInfo()` / `GetTotalCallCount()` and closure-based request/header capture, both
  outside and inside a bubble.
- An unregistered method (e.g. POST when only GET is registered) fails closed with `"no responder
  found for method ..."` rather than silently succeeding — useful for proving a write request never
  reached a live server.

This matches expectation: `MockTransport.RoundTrip` is a plain synchronous, in-process call with no
goroutines, timers, or sockets of its own, so it imposes nothing on the bubble that the bubble
doesn't already control. It does **not** by itself solve the *custom timing behavior* several of
this repo's tests need (see below) — that behavior is written in the responder function either way.

## Survey of the current HTTP test fakes

| Package | File(s) | Mechanism | `httptest.NewServer` calls |
|---|---|---|---|
| `internal/firefly` | `accounts_test.go` | `pagedAccountsServer` helper + `writeJSON` | 4 |
| `internal/firefly` | `transactions_test.go` | `pagedTxServer` helper | 3 |
| `internal/firefly` | `readonly_test.go` | `countingServer` helper + 2 bare servers (redirect, header-capture) | 3 |
| `internal/bank/enablebanking` | `transactions_test.go` | per-test bare servers, one hand-rolled `fixedResponseRoundTripper` for a synctest-adjacent retry-cap case | 7 |
| `internal/bank/enablebanking` | `auth_test.go` | per-test bare servers (JWT/OAuth exchange) | 6 |
| `internal/notify/telegram` | `telegram_test.go` | custom `fakeTelegram` (`http.RoundTripper`), scripted per-chat replies, synctest timing (min 1.1s gap, flood-control `retry_after` in body) | 2 (only for non-timing cases) |
| `internal/httpx` | `retry_test.go`, `client_test.go` | custom `fakeTransport` (`http.RoundTripper`): scripted steps incl. `hang` (blocks on `req.Context().Done()`), `stallBody` (blocks every `Read`), exact per-attempt timestamps, capped-drain probe body | 0 (synctest-only, `.claude/CLAUDE.md` explicitly forbids sockets here) |
| `internal/app` | `readonly_test.go` | `roRecorder` wrapping a real `http.Handler`, two live `httptest.Server`s dialed through `app.RunEnv`'s real config `baseURL`s | 2 |
| `internal/app` | `privacy_test.go` | live `httptest.Server` (Telegram) + hand-rolled SMTP server over a self-signed TLS listener, both dialed through `app.RunEnv` | 1 (+ raw `net`/`tls` listener for SMTP) |

## Per-package assessment

### `internal/firefly` — adopt

`New(baseURL, token string, base http.RoundTripper, opts ...Option)` already takes an injectable
`http.RoundTripper` as its base transport (wrapped by `ReadOnlyTransport` then
`httpx.RetryTransport` then `httpx.NewClient`). There is no dependency on a *real* listener: every
test only inspects what the client sent and controls what it receives. httpmock's
`ResponderFromMultipleResponses` is a direct replacement for the hand-rolled
`pagedAccountsServer`/`pagedTxServer` "serve body N on request N" pattern, and
`RegisterResponderWithQuery`/closures replace `writeJSON` + manual `url.Values` capture.

Before (`internal/firefly/accounts_test.go`, current):

```go
func (s *AccountsSuite) pagedAccountsServer(bodies ...[]byte) (*httptest.Server, *[]url.Values) {
	queries := make([]url.Values, 0, len(bodies))
	terminal := s.fixture("accounts_nometa.json")

	server := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		queries = append(queries, r.URL.Query())
		idx := len(queries) - 1
		if idx < len(bodies) {
			writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, bodies[idx])
			return
		}
		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, terminal)
	}))

	return server, &queries
}

func (s *AccountsSuite) TestListAccountsRequestsAssetTypeLimit500AndOwnPageCounter() {
	p1 := s.fixture("accounts_p1.json")
	p2 := s.fixture("accounts_p2.json")

	server, queries := s.pagedAccountsServer(p1, p2)
	defer server.Close()

	client := New(server.URL, "token", http.DefaultTransport)

	got, err := client.ListAccounts(context.Background())
	s.Require().NoError(err)
	s.Len(got, 7)
	s.Require().Len(*queries, 2)
	s.Equal(url.Values{"type": {"asset"}, "limit": {"500"}, "page": {"1"}}, (*queries)[0])
	s.Equal(url.Values{"type": {"asset"}, "limit": {"500"}, "page": {"2"}}, (*queries)[1])
}
```

After (with `httpmock`):

```go
func (s *AccountsSuite) TestListAccountsRequestsAssetTypeLimit500AndOwnPageCounter() {
	transport := httpmock.NewMockTransport()
	var queries []url.Values

	transport.RegisterResponder("GET", `=~^http://firefly\.test/accounts`,
		func(req *http.Request) (*http.Response, error) {
			queries = append(queries, req.URL.Query())
			body := s.fixture("accounts_nometa.json")
			if len(queries) == 1 {
				body = s.fixture("accounts_p1.json")
			} else if len(queries) == 2 {
				body = s.fixture("accounts_p2.json")
			}
			return httpmock.NewBytesResponse(http.StatusOK, body), nil
		})

	client := New("http://firefly.test", "token", transport)

	got, err := client.ListAccounts(context.Background())
	s.Require().NoError(err)
	s.Len(got, 7)
	s.Require().Len(queries, 2)
	s.Equal(url.Values{"type": {"asset"}, "limit": {"500"}, "page": {"1"}}, queries[0])
	s.Equal(url.Values{"type": {"asset"}, "limit": {"500"}, "page": {"2"}}, queries[1])
}
```

(`ResponderFromMultipleResponses` is a cleaner fit than the `if/else` above when the terminal page
never needs to repeat; a small closure is shown here because this suite's helper deliberately
serves an unbounded terminal page to prove the 200-page safety cap can't hang.)

Net effect across the package: removes `pagedAccountsServer` (~18 lines), `pagedTxServer`
(~20 lines), `countingServer` (~10 lines, used 3×) and two bare `httptest.NewServer` blocks in
`readonly_test.go` (redirect + header-capture cases, ~20 lines combined), plus every
`defer server.Close()` / `server.URL` wiring line at each of the ~14 call sites. Estimated
~70–90 lines of scaffolding removed, replaced by ~25–35 lines of `httpmock` registration. It also
removes a latent, if harmless-in-practice, data race: `httptest.Server` runs each request in its
own goroutine, so `queries = append(queries, ...)` in the current helpers is only race-free because
these clients happen to be sequential; a `MockTransport` round trip runs synchronously in the
caller's own goroutine, so that carefulness is no longer load-bearing.

`readonly_test.go`'s `TestGetDoesNotFollowRedirect` (two servers, A redirects to B) still works:
register one responder returning `NewStringResponse` with `StatusFound` and a `Location` header for
`http://firefly.test/`, a second responder for the "B" URL, and assert the second responder's call
count is 0. `http.Client`'s redirect-following logic (`CheckRedirect`) runs one layer above the
transport, so it observes a mocked 3xx exactly as it would a real one.

### `internal/bank/enablebanking` — adopt

Same shape as `firefly`: per-test bare `httptest.Server`s recording path/query/headers for JWT
client-credentials exchange and paginated transaction fetches, plus one already-bespoke
`fixedResponseRoundTripper` (a hand-rolled zero-dependency mock transport that duplicates exactly
what `httpmock.NewStringResponder` + a header does) that `httpmock` would replace outright:

Before:

```go
type fixedResponseRoundTripper struct {
	status     int
	retryAfter string
}

func (rt *fixedResponseRoundTripper) RoundTrip(req *http.Request) (*http.Response, error) {
	header := make(http.Header)
	if rt.retryAfter != "" {
		header.Set("Retry-After", rt.retryAfter)
	}
	return &http.Response{
		StatusCode: rt.status, Header: header,
		Body: io.NopCloser(strings.NewReader("")), Request: req,
	}, nil
}
```

After:

```go
transport := httpmock.NewMockTransport()
resp := httpmock.NewStringResponse(http.StatusTooManyRequests, "")
resp.Header.Set("Retry-After", "120")
transport.RegisterResponder("GET", `=~.*`, httpmock.ResponderFromResponse(resp))
```

13 `httptest.NewServer` call sites across the two files; expect a similar ~60–70% reduction in
scaffolding lines to `internal/firefly`. No case in either file needs a real listener, TLS, or a
body-read timeout — they assert request shape and response mapping only.

### `internal/notify/telegram` — adopt for the non-timing cases only

`telegram_test.go`'s `fakeTelegram` combines two responsibilities: (a) decoding the request body
and recording `chatID`/`text`/`url`, and (b) scripting per-chat reply sequences including
flood-control (`429` with `retry_after` in the *body*, not a header) and exact-timestamp assertions
under `synctest`. (a) is what `httpmock` is for — `ResponderFromMultipleResponses` keyed by a
`RegisterMatcherResponder` on `chat_id` in the body would replace the `script`/`calls` map — but
(b) is the same category as `internal/httpx`'s retry tests: the value is in the *timing* assertion
(`minPartGap`, exact `retry_after` waits), which requires the same custom logic to capture
`time.Now()` per call regardless of which registration API wraps it. Recommend leaving this file as
is rather than a split migration that would make one package inconsistent between two idioms for no
real line reduction; revisit only if/when the timing suite is refactored for other reasons.

### `internal/httpx` — keep

`fakeTransport` supports `hang` (block until `req.Context().Done()`, then fail with the context
error) and `stallBody` (block every `Body.Read`), used to prove the 30s per-attempt timeout bounds
both connect and body-read phases, and it records an exact `time.Time` per attempt to pin the
1s/2s/4s backoff schedule. `httpmock` responders are plain functions, so this behavior *could* be
written as an `httpmock.Responder` closure — but it would be the same amount of code (the hang/stall
logic doesn't shrink), just relocated from a `RoundTrip` method to a registered closure, while
losing the current file's single self-contained `fakeTransport` type that both `retry_test.go` and
`client_test.go` already share. No net benefit; `.claude/CLAUDE.md`'s explicit "in-process fake
`http.RoundTripper`" guidance for this file is already httpmock-compatible in principle (per the
spike above) but not httpmock-*motivated* — keep the hand-written fake.

### `internal/app` (`readonly_test.go`, `privacy_test.go`) — keep `httptest.Server`

These are genuine end-to-end tests: `app.RunEnv` is invoked with `app.BuildDeps` unmodified, so it
builds its own real `http.Client`s and dials the `baseURL`/`EnableBankingBaseURL` the harness wrote
into a temp config file or `Env`. There is no test-visible `http.RoundTripper` injection point here
by design — the point of the suite is to prove the *real* client stack (DNS/dial to `127.0.0.1`,
real header serialization) never sends a write method or a `Psu-*` header. `privacy_test.go`
additionally drives a hand-rolled SMTP server behind a real, self-signed-TLS `net.Listener`, which
is not HTTP at all. `httpmock` only intercepts `http.RoundTripper`; it cannot stand in for a real
listening socket without either replacing `http.DefaultTransport` globally (explicitly the unsafe,
non-parallel-safe mode the bead's design note warns against) or plumbing a new transport-injection
seam through `app.BuildDeps` that does not exist today and would weaken exactly the "drove through
the real client" guarantee these tests exist to provide. Correctly out of scope.

## Risks if adopted

- Two idioms will coexist in the repo (`httpmock` in `firefly`/`enablebanking`, hand-rolled fakes in
  `httpx`/`telegram`/`app`) — acceptable and precedented (`testify` suites already coexist with
  plain assertions were they used, and `.claude/CLAUDE.md` already distinguishes "HTTP adapters
  tested against `httptest.Server`" from "synctest-safe in-process fake" as different tools for
  different jobs); document the split once in that file's Testing section if adopted, so a future
  contributor doesn't try to force one idiom everywhere.
- `RegisterResponder`'s default URL matching ignores query string by default for the plain-string
  form (query is matched separately unless a `=~` regex is used) — migration must double-check each
  test's query-matching still asserts what it asserts today, not just that *a* response comes back.
- `go.sum` will gain the two indirect entries even though nothing is compiled from them (see Facts);
  worth a one-line note in a future `chore:` commit so it isn't mistaken for scope creep in a
  vulnerability scan.

## If adopted

Owner approval needed first (test-only dependency, `github.com/stretchr/testify` is the precedent).
File one migration bead per package: `internal/firefly`, `internal/bank/enablebanking` — each is a
self-contained, mechanical swap of `httptest.Server` helpers for `httpmock.MockTransport`
responders with no production-code change, following the before/after shape above.

title: Migrate the retry loop in internal/httpx onto github.com/avast/retry-go v5
description: Owner approved retry-go (fj-91d.6 decision). Replace the hand-written attempt loop and wait timer in internal/httpx/retry.go with retry-go, keeping every guarantee the current tests pin.
design: Dependency: github.com/avast/retry-go/v5 at its latest release (v5.0.0 or newer, released >= 2025-01-01; confirm with ctx7 docs and the module proxy). Read the fj-91d.6 spike comment first (br show fj-91d.6): the guarantee table lists what retry-go gives natively (attempt count, context cancellation) and what stays ours: converting retryable responses (network error, any 5xx, 429) into a typed error carrying the Retry-After delay; backoff 1/2/4 s with ±20% injectable jitter via a custom DelayType; Retry-After (seconds or HTTP-date via http.ParseTime) replaces backoff; cap 60 s with over-cap -> retry.Unrecoverable(&RetryAfterTooLongError{}) so errors.As still works; only bodyless GET/HEAD enter the retry path, everything else passes straight through; LastErrorOnly(true) so errors are not concatenated; the last response is handed back to the caller after the final attempt (own attempt counter / stash); discarded bodies drained with the 64 KiB cap; context cancellation during waits. TimeoutTransport and NewClient are unchanged. TDD: the existing RetrySuite/ClientSuite tests are the contract — they must pass unchanged or be ported one-to-one (same scenarios, same assertions, same synctest timings); add a test first for any behaviour the library could change (e.g. no concatenated multi-attempt error text, no stderr output). No sockets inside synctest. Update .claude/CLAUDE.md Dependencies (retry-go approved, what it is for; drop 'no retry library'), research.md R12 (decision and alternatives considered: go-retryablehttp rejected with the spike's reasons), plan.md if it lists dependencies. go mod tidy; task audit clean.
acceptance_criteria: Retry loop runs on retry-go; all previous httpx behaviour tests pass (unchanged or ported one-to-one, listed in the report); errors.As(RetryAfterTooLongError) and last-response hand-back still hold; no new stderr output; CLAUDE.md, research R12 (and plan.md if needed) updated; govulncheck clean. task check exits 0; one Conventional Commit on main, subject and body only, no trailers; .golangci.yml unchanged; no other project names or local paths in tracked files.
